rows.note: Use 會 as the all-purpose future auxiliary for future events or intentions.

example.english: I will go to work earlier tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ting1 jat6 wui5 zou2 di1 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken choice for a person's intention, decision, or wishes.

example.english: My will is to stay home tonight.
example.traditional: 我嘅意思係今晚唔出街。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ge3 ji3 si1 hai6 gam1 maan5 m4 ceot1 gaai1

rows.note: Use 肯 when asking or stating whether someone is willing to agree to do something.

example.english: Will you agree to look after my things for me?
example.jyutping: nei5 hang2 bong1 ngo5 tai2 zyu6 di1 je5 maa3

rows.note: Use this for an abstract faculty of choice or a strong inner will, especially in expressions such as 求生意志.

example.english: They got through the operation with sheer will.
example.traditional: 佢靠住強大嘅意志捱過咗手術。
example.jyutping: keoi5 kaau3 zyu6 koeng4 daai6 ge3 ji3 zi3 ngaai4 gwo3 zo2 sau2 seot6

rows.note: Use this when the will means firm determination or a settled resolve to do something.

example.english: My will to quit smoking is strong.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gaai3 jin1 ge3 kyut3 sam1 hou2 gin1 ding6

rows.note: Use this for the formal legal document stating how a person's property should be distributed after death.

example.english: Grandpa made a will before he died, specifying who would get the flat.
example.traditional: 爺爺生前立咗遺囑，講明間屋留畀邊個。
example.jyutping: je4 je4 sang1 cin4 lap6 zo2 wai4 zuk1 gong2 ming4 gaan1 uk1 lau4 bei2 bin1 go3
